digest.component_or_area: DC parent hierarchy reconciliation, outbound field diffing and emission
propositions: A non-epic parent in outbound diffing returns (False, None) indistinguishably from an unbound parent, so the suppression never generates a bridge alert or enters the divergence-recording apparatus, and the pass exits 0 reporting convergence while the hierarchy actually diverges.

The three originally failing test cells were wrong oracles asserting operations the platform cannot perform (sub-task parent mutation via fields.parent is accept-and-ignore by DC), not symptoms of the rebar defect.

The supported parent mechanism is the Epic Link custom field on a non-sub-task child, which reconcile passes already carry successfully; re-homing the three cells to this mechanism preserves their user-visible contract while fixing the oracle.

When a user sets a parent that rebar cannot represent for a child shape, rebar must emit a durable operator-visible signal (bridge alert naming the reason and supported alternative) instead of silently dropping the field.
The convergence gate must compare the suppressed local parent against the remote parent to avoid spurious alerts on already-converged tickets where the tracker legitimately holds a non-epic parent.
